prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1257; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representing attorney following a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Initial notice received and file opened for bodily injury and property damage review.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. It documents the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the time of the impact and records the other driver's account of the incident.

Entry 3: Recorded statement taken from the other driver, who describes the same sequence of events as the claimant and confirms the vehicle was stationary and then struck from behind while backing out of a space.

Entry 4: Photographs from the scene and the vehicle's rear bumper and trunk area were received. The visible damage is mostly in line with the impact described and appears consistent with the reported speed of contact.

Entry 5: Two independent witnesses contacted this office. Both confirm the collision occurred as described and that the claimant was seated in the vehicle when it happened.

Entry 6: Verified that the driver is listed as a named driver on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 7: Prior-loss and repair history checked for the vehicle. No earlier damage to this area is known, and no previous claims were found on the vehicle.

Entry 8: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The reported whiplash injury fits the type and force of this kind of impact, and the diagnosis and imaging notes are in line with that mechanism.

Entry 9: Claimant's attorney provided a prior medical summary. It notes a minor strain to the same region several years ago that resolved completely with routine care, and it does not appear to bear on the current complaints.

Entry 10: Treatment history reviewed. Care followed a typical course, with frequency of visits tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved. A later written statement added a few minor details about the moments after impact, but the core account has remained unchanged across all contacts.

Entry 11: File reviewed and assessed for evaluation. Liability and damage facts are supported by the police report, witnesses, photographs and the other driver. Injury claim proceeding to evaluation based on the medical course and the documented mechanism of injury.
